_strings.@@36ebbb27b540: Treaty conformity — NC conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from NC income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the NC return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: NC conforms. The 2023 D-401 instructions state on Line 6: "The starting point for determining North Carolina taxable income is federal adjusted gross income." Because federally treaty-exempt income is already excluded from federal AGI, it flows through to NC untaxed UNLESS NC adds it back. The complete list of Form D-400 Schedule S, Part A "Additions to Federal Adjusted Gross Income" (Lines 1-16, D-401 pp. 17-18) contains NO add-back of treaty-exempt income (additions are limited to items like non-NC state/local bond interest, bonus depreciation, IRC 179 expense, Opportunity Fund deferred gains, S-corp built-in gains, federal NOL, 529 withdrawals, employer education-loan payments, expenses allocable to exempt income, etc.). Since treaty-exempt income is not re-taxed, conforms_to_federal_treaties = true. Note one nuance to flag for filers: Schedule S Part A Line 12 requires adding back EXPENSES allocable to income exempt from NC tax, but it does not add back the exempt income itself.

_strings.@@816074f82659: Credit for Income Tax Paid to Another State or Country — N.C. residents (and part-year residents for the resident period) only. Available when income earned while a legal resident of North Carolina is taxed by both North Carolina and another U.S. state or a foreign country because it was earned in or derived from sources in that other state/country. No credit for tax paid to a city/county/other political subdivision or to the federal government. Nonresidents are NOT entitled to this credit. A copy of the return filed with the other state/country and proof of payment must be attached.

_strings.@@ac1de4204fcd: Tax Credit for Rehabilitating Historic Structures (Articles 3D / 3H / 3L) — Narrow / not broadly applicable to ordinary residents. Available to taxpayers who incur qualified rehabilitation expenditures/expenses on a certified historic structure or historic mill facility placed in service under the requirements of Article 3D (expired for expenditures incurred by Jan 1, 2023; property must have been placed in service by Jan 1, 2023), Article 3H (historic mill facility; requires eligibility certification from the State Historic Preservation Officer), or Article 3L (current Historic Rehabilitation Tax Credits Investment Program; requires Form NC-Rehab). Distinguishes income-producing vs. non-income-producing structures.

state_tax.work_common_tail: 0. Tax line: D-400 Line 15: multiply Line 14 (N.C. taxable income, full-year residents) by the income tax rate of 4.75% (0.0475). Line 6 starts from federal AGI; Line 14 = federal AGI + additions - deductions - child deduction (Line 10) - N.C. standard/itemized deduction (Line 11). This op computes the state's flat-rate tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: Standard-deduction gates NOT modeled by calc.state_tax: MFS gets $0 if the spouse itemizes, and the N.C. standard deduction is ZERO for anyone not eligible for the FEDERAL standard deduction (the chart lists nonresident aliens at $0) — itemizers use D-400 Line 12 instead; compute those cases on the form. N.C. child deduction (D-400 Line 10) is NOT modeled: up to $3,000 per qualifying child (a child allowed the federal child tax credit), stepping down $3,000/$2,500/$2,000/$1,500/$1,000/$500/$0 by federal AGI (MFJ brackets up to $40,000 ... over $140,000; HoH up to $30,000 ... over $105,000; Single/MFS up to $20,000 ... over $70,000) — take it from the D-401 table, not from a per-dependent exemption. North Carolina has no personal or dependent exemptions.
